title: Cheese and Roasted Capsicum Burekas
subtitle: with a laminated butter dough
description: Triangular burekas made from a homemade laminated butter dough (kosher for Passover flour blend) filled with a baking cheese mixture and roasted capsicum. The dough needs at least nine hours of chilling in total.

steps.text: Make the dough: in a mixer bowl with a dough hook combine 650 g of the flour blend, xanthan gum and salt, then add the icing sugar and glucose. Cube 100 g of the butter and add it to the mixer; knead until the butter is well coated in flour. Add the water, sour cream, 1 egg yolk and vinegar and knead until smooth. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.

Make the butter block: cube the remaining 450 g butter and mix with the remaining 50 g of flour blend in the mixer on medium speed until creamy and smooth. Shape between sheets of baking paper into a 20 x 20 cm square and refrigerate.

Roll the dough out in four directions, from the centre outwards, to a 40 x 40 cm square. Place the butter block in the centre and fold the four corners over it like an envelope, making sure the butter is fully enclosed. The butter and dough should be equally firm.

Roll the dough to 80 cm long and fold it in thirds. Freeze for about 3 hours. Turn the dough so the fold is on the side, roll to 120 cm, fold each side quarter over quarter, then fold in half. Freeze for 2 hours. Roll and fold twice more in the same order. Let the dough rest for another 2 hours (or overnight) in the freezer.
Mix the filling ingredients (baking cheese, cornflour, 2 eggs, black pepper and 6 g fine salt) until smooth.
Roll the dough to about 1/2 cm thick and cut 15 x 15 cm squares, ideally with a pizza cutter. Place filling in the centre of each square, add roasted capsicum, and fold diagonally to form a triangle.
Brush with beaten egg and the remaining yolk and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Place on a tray lined with baking paper and freeze until baking.
Take the burekas out of the freezer 20 minutes before baking. Start baking at 190°C and after 5 minutes reduce to 160°C for another 20 minutes, until deep golden brown.
